proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem 4 gives fixed-rule-dimensional asymptotic normality and a quadratic regret limit under compact covariate support, bounded rule derivatives, and low-dimensional or sufficiently rich balancing-sieve conditions.
Nonparametrically estimated-propensity IPW attains the semiparametric efficiency bound for the average treatment effect under its rich-score conditions.
The proportional logistic MLE has coordinate and norm limits governed by a finite state system for one convex likelihood problem.
Logistic-MLE existence has a sharp Gaussian proportional phase-transition curve.
A convex Gaussian M-estimator has a deterministic squared-error limit obtained from a finite scalar saddle problem.
A quadratic approximate-balance constraint avoids infeasibility of high-dimensional exact balancing.
The approximate kinematic formula locates random cone-intersection transitions through statistical dimensions up to a square-root-dimensional window.
Entropy balancing has an exponential-tilt dual whose optimum enforces exact covariate moments.
Entropy balancing is doubly robust and can attain semiparametric efficiency under fixed-dimensional model conditions.
A debiased proportional regression adjustment admits a linear-plus-quadratic limit and feasible conservative inference.
Doubly robust policy scores support regret guarantees for empirical policy learning under observational sampling.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct and prove a finite deterministic same-sample tilt-policy resolvent with exhaustive global selection for all three nonconcave policy objectives, and establish the boundary-uniform localization needed for the proportional small-aspect constants.
open_obligations.obstruction: The exact equations retain two entropy tilts, all tilt-policy overlaps, and block-Jacobian own-row responses. The logistic parameterization makes the empirical policy criterion nonconcave, so stationary fixed points neither identify the lexicographically selected global norm nor exclude branch coexistence. The fixed-dimensional theorem supplies no uniformity as dimension grows.
open_obligations.attempted: The exact finite-sample balance and radius-KKT equations, the conic feasibility phase, radial regret reduction, fixed-dimensional global M-estimator law, exact entropy quadratic identity, and a feasible-side conditional-energy floor were derived. Convex Gaussian minimax and independent-weight surrogates were rejected because their hypotheses or estimators differ from the frozen same-sample construction.

prose_updates.tldr: In the binary Gaussian randomized-trial calibration, population regret is exactly a strictly increasing function of the selected policy norm, while only the marginal true-propensity objective law is independent of \(\gamma\). The established proportional result is the exact pooled-target entropy-balance feasibility threshold \(\kappa_{\mathrm{bal}}=0.3043687064\ldots\), which exceeds the fixed-zero-target orthant threshold \(1/4\). The entropy strong-penalty quadratic has an explicit positive conditional-energy floor throughout the feasible region and a two-sided order bracket with leverage concentration only at sufficiently small aspect ratio. In fixed policy dimension, all three global estimators are localized at zero, have explicit normal limits, and satisfy the strict covariance ordering \(\Sigma_D\prec\Sigma_E\prec\Sigma_T\). A proportional same-sample deterministic norm system, regret ranking, radius cells, and unconditional phase inference remain open.

project_justification.gap: FangRidderXie2026 proves its benchmark-lottery result under fixed rule dimension, compact covariate support, bounded rule derivatives, and a low-dimensional or sufficiently rich balancing sieve. Those conditions do not contain the present unbounded Gaussian design, proportional dimension, and exact balance only on \((1,q^\top)^\top\). Existing proportional logistic and convex Gaussian results do not handle two endogenous same-sample entropy tilts followed by a nonconcave global policy selector.
project_justification.niche: The proved package isolates what survives without the missing joint system: a deformed-orthant pooled-target feasibility threshold, a global feasible-side conditional-energy floor, a small-aspect order bracket for the original entropy weights, and a complete fixed-dimensional M-estimation limit with exact score-covariance ordering. It does not infer a proportional regret sign from numerical fits or from fixed-dimensional variances.
project_justification.fill: The note currently delivers the exact threshold comparison \(1/4\) versus \(0.3043687064\ldots\), the fixed-dimensional normal and quadratic-regret limit laws, and rigorous entropy-quadratic bounds. The remaining research target is an explicitly open proportional-Gaussian analogue for the binary benchmark-logit specialization: it must retain same-row tilt-policy Jacobians and certify the selected global branches before any HIR cells or plug-in phase labels are asserted.

prose_updates.related_work: FangRidderXie2026 supplies the benchmark-lottery motivation and a fixed-rule-dimensional regret theorem under compact support, bounded rule derivatives, and balancing-sieve conditions; the present fixed-dimensional theorem is a binary benchmark-one-half Gaussian specialization and calibration, while the open proportional target is an analogue rather than a strict class extension. HiranoImbensRidder2003 supplies the rich estimated-propensity score-projection mechanism, whereas the exact covariance calculation here shows that balancing only the same linear coordinates is strictly between true IPW and oracle DR. SurCandes2019 treats one proportional logistic likelihood, and ThrampoulidisAbbasiHassibi2018 treats convex Gaussian estimators; neither certifies two endogenous entropy tilts followed by this nonconcave global selector. CandesSur2020 and AmelunxenLotzMcCoyTropp2014 provide separation and conic tools for the pooled-target threshold. Hainmueller2012 and ZhaoPercival2017 concern entropy duality and fixed-dimensional efficiency, while DaiYan2024 studies high-dimensional balance feasibility. LuYangWang2025 motivates leverage-aware proportional adjustments but does not cover these endogenous exponential tilts. AtheyWager2021 supplies the oracle-DR policy-score comparator. AshrafKarlanYin2006 is the motivating application, not a claim that its data satisfy this binary Gaussian calibration model.
prose_updates.interpretation: Balancing an arm of asymptotic size \(n/2\) to a fixed zero target has the ordinary threshold \(p/n=1/4\); balancing it to the pooled empirical mean correlates the target with the arm rows and raises the exact threshold to \(0.3043687064\ldots\). Below that boundary, exact weights exist with high probability, but existence alone does not determine whether their downstream policy regret is smaller than true-propensity IPW. The fixed-dimensional limit proves a strict partial efficiency gain, not a proportional ranking.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The all-feasible-aspect lower floor follows from an exact Gram and Cauchy--Schwarz inequality plus the Gaussian spectral edge, but the matching upper bound and leverage concentration are proved only for sufficiently small \(\kappa\). Neither result identifies a deterministic coefficient. More importantly, the joint same-row response matrices for the entropy tilts and policy scores have no proved finite deterministic closure, and the empirical logistic-policy criterion need not be globally concave. Stationary roots therefore cannot certify the lexicographically selected global optimizer, radius transitions, or collision gaps. The fixed-dimensional normal law does not supply the boundary-uniform localization or limit interchange needed for proportional small-aspect regret constants.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Established results are the radial regret identity, marginal true-IPW \(\gamma\)-invariance, the exact pooled-target feasibility threshold and its fixed-zero-target \(1/4\) comparison, a complete fixed-dimensional global M-estimator and quadratic-regret limit law with \(\Sigma_D\prec\Sigma_E\prec\Sigma_T\), the exact entropy conditional quadratic identity, its Bernoulli fluctuation bound, the global feasible-side conditional-energy floor, and a small-aspect order bracket with vanishing leverage criterion. Exact-balance conclusions remain restricted to \(\mathcal E_{0n}\cap\mathcal E_{1n}\cap\mathcal Q_n\); the uniform complement rule only totalizes finite-sample outputs. No proportional deterministic regret limit, leading small-aspect regret coefficient, positive/zero/negative HIR cell, ranking reversal, radius boundary, or nonempty certified inference stratum is proved. Conditional phase inference remains valid only if a nonabstaining differentiable certified branch neighborhood is constructed independently. Learned outcome regression, non-Gaussian covariates, heterogeneous effects, multiple arms, and a literal model of the commitment-savings outcomes remain outside scope.

statement_notes.consumer: The two normalizations tell analysts when exact same-coordinate balancing is unavailable before any policy comparison is attempted.
